title: Lovers on the Celestial Sphere
identity: Jun Nagao’s Lovers on the Celestial Sphere is Zen-On 560015 for soprano saxophone, tenor saxophone and piano, composed on commission from Nobuya Sugawa. Zen-On gives about 12 minutes, while an institutional catalog gives about 12.5 for the later band study score. Zen-On’s public four-page sample includes a preface and an opening score leaf.

evidence.claim: Lists scoring as soprano saxophone, tenor saxophone and piano, approximately 12 minutes.
Study score is the wind-band version; records original performance medium as soprano/tenor saxophone and piano, approximately 12.5 minutes.
Lists the piece for soprano and tenor saxophones and piano.
Album listing credits the work and pianist Kazuo Murakami.

Zen-On product 560015 confirms the commissioned soprano/tenor/piano work, first performance in 2005 by Nobuya Sugawa, Sadahito Kuniuse and pianist Minako Koyanagi, and an approximate 12-minute duration.
Opened Zen-On’s public ActiBook sample (4 pages). The preface identifies the 2005 premiere and the opening printed score leaf was visually inspected.
A NASA conference program search result lists the work in a collegiate solo competition event; the PDF URL returned 404 on opening, so the program context remains indexed-only.

score_observations: The opening sample page shows soprano and tenor parts over piano, marked Con espressione at a slow pulse, with legato saxophone lines and a flowing, chordal piano texture. The sample does not show enough of the work to infer complete range or later movement demands.
review_focus: Inference from the inspected opening: assess blend between the two saxophone lines and the flowing piano texture, then review later handoffs and contrasts in the complete edition.
collection_flag: Original saxophone duo with piano; separately available wind-band study score is not the original trio format.

score_links.description: Official four-page Zen-On ActiBook sample; opening score leaf visually inspected.

gaps: Only an opening score leaf and preface were available in the public sample; the remainder of the duo score was not inspected.
The later band study-score timing differs slightly from Zen-On’s original chamber-work estimate.
